claims.text: Extreme lattice distortion is present in the high-entropy alloy.
Lattice distortion nearly balances vacancy and interstitial mobilities during cyclic mechanical loading.
Balanced point-defect mobilities enhance in situ defect recombination.
Enhanced recombination suppresses defect clustering and stable dislocation pile-ups.
Suppression of defect clusters and dislocation pile-ups delays fatigue-crack initiation.
The proposed mechanism gives high-entropy alloys a superior strength-ductility balance under dynamic loading relative to low-entropy alloys.
Nominally equiatomic NbTaTiV is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
NbTaTiV has a highly disordered elemental distribution and significant lattice distortion.
The NbTaTiV BCC solid-solution phase remains stable from room temperature through approximately 700 degrees Celsius.
The proposed mechanism should operate under cyclic loading from room temperature to approximately 700 degrees Celsius if the alloy remains single-phase and disordered.
The high-entropy alloy will have a higher strain-hardening rate during dynamic loading than the low-entropy control.
The high-entropy alloy will have a lower fatigue-crack-initiation rate than the low-entropy control.
The high-entropy alloy will survive more cycles before failure than the low-entropy control.
A W-Ta-V-Cr refractory high-entropy alloy showed no irradiation-created dislocation loops under the reported irradiation conditions.
The controlled comparison should use an HEA and a binary or ternary BCC alloy with similar average composition but lower configurational entropy and lattice distortion.
Both material sets should undergo identical cyclic tests over multiple strain rates and temperatures, with stress-strain behavior, crack initiation, cycle life, and defect structures measured.
Failure to observe improved strain hardening, delayed crack initiation, or increased cycle life in the HEA would falsify the hypothesis.
